title: Tech 07 Deploy Rollback
decision: Choose rollout and rollback policy for a high-risk service release.
context: A release changes request routing and database access patterns.
The service is latency-sensitive and globally distributed.
The change cannot be perfectly simulated in staging.
constraints: Customer error rate must not exceed 1 percent for more than five minutes.
Rollback must not require a schema downgrade.
The rollout should reach all traffic within one business day if healthy.
options: Deploy globally at once with manual monitoring.
Use staged canaries with automatic abort thresholds and backward-compatible schema changes.
Hold the release until a production-identical staging environment exists.

evidence.fact: The previous three routing regressions were detectable in error rate or p95 latency within four minutes.
The new schema fields are additive and the old application version ignores them safely.
A 1 percent traffic canary produces enough volume for statistically useful latency signals in about 12 minutes.
Global rollback of the application version completes in nine minutes.
Building a production-identical staging environment is estimated to take six weeks and still would not reproduce third-party latency variance.
Feature flags can disable the new routing path without redeploying, but database read-pattern changes still require application rollback.
